commands.collect: uv run --frozen --project harness python scripts/s3/sqruff_rules.py collect
commands.sources: uv run --frozen --project harness python scripts/s3/sqruff_rules.py sources
commands.build: uv run --frozen --project harness python scripts/s3/sqruff_rules.py build

scope.note: The rules, autofix, and templater failures of known_failures/sqruff.txt (the S1 sqruff run; T2 per-case list results/s3/sqruff-cases.json).

method: Each failure has one class, in this order. 1. unsupported_item: the reason of known_failures/sqruff.txt is 'unsupported: <item>'; the group comes from the item. 2. parse_cause: a SQL file that a failed check reads (rules: pass_str reads pass, fail_str and fix read fail, after_fix reads fixed; a case with no failed check, a tool error, reads all its files; autofix: before.sql; templater: the case file) has another tree in sqruff than in sqlfluff (sqruff-rule-parses.json: the sqruff and sqlfluff parse of the file with the case config and with the meta segments). For rules and autofix, the meta type 'implicit' of sqruff is 'indent', the type that sqlfluff gives to ImplicitIndent. For templater, the suite compares the type names, so 'implicit' is a difference. 3. rule_logic: the other failures: the trees are equal, so the rule, fix, or config logic of sqruff gives another result. A tree difference does not prove that it causes the failure: the estimate 'touch' gives how many parse_cause cases change a type that the rule reads.

classes.unsupported_item: The case uses an item that sqruff does not support: a setting, a rule, a dialect, an output field, or a value that its INI config cannot hold. The harness does not run the case (harness/sqruff.md, 'Unsupported items'). This class comes first: the other causes are not known.
classes.parse_cause: A SQL file that a failed check reads has another sqruff tree than the sqlfluff tree: another tree, an unparsable node, or no tree (sqruff cannot template the file). The trees are compared with the meta segments, as the rules see them.
classes.rule_logic: The SQL files that the failed checks read have the same tree in sqruff and in sqlfluff. Thus the rule, fix, or config logic of sqruff gives another result (also a sqruff panic). Kind 'config value panic': sqruff panics on a config value of the case before a rule runs: the parse of the case SQL also panics with the case config, and passes without the rules and layout sections. These cases are near to an unsupported item (a setting value); 'sensitivity' gives the counts with them in unsupported_item.

judgement: The class of each case follows the rule of 'method'; the unsupported_item counts are measurements. The split between parse_cause and rule_logic depends on 2 choices (the meta name 'implicit' and the files of the failed checks): 'sensitivity' gives the counts with the other choices. The rule_logic cases of kind 'config value panic' fail on a config value, not in the rule; they stay in rule_logic because the harness runs them (they are not 'unsupported:' in known_failures/sqruff.txt). 'sensitivity' gives the counts with them in unsupported_item. That a tree difference causes the failure is an estimate ('touch').

sensitivity.note: The class counts (all suites) with another rule. implicit_differs: 'implicit' is a tree difference also for rules and autofix. all_files: each file of a rule case, not only the files of the failed checks. config_value_panic_as_unsupported: the rule_logic cases of kind 'config value panic' are unsupported_item. Estimates: they show how much the counts depend on these choices.

by_rule_note: by_rule: the key is the rule list of a case: rules: the rule codes of the case (can be a list); autofix: the rules of test-config.yml, or 'all'; templater: '-'. by_rule_code: for each single code, the cases whose rule list has the code; a case with N codes counts N times.

touch.note: An estimate of the share of parse_cause cases (rules and autofix) where the tree difference is a likely cause. A rule does not see a statement that sqruff does not parse or template. A difference that changes no name that the rule reads can still change its result (for example through the position of a meta or a parent).

coupling.method: names: the segment types that a rule reads (TYPES_FILE: the SyntaxKind names of its file and of its helper modules, and the layout config types for the reflow rules). The base segment module sqruff-lib-core/parser/segments.rs is not a helper module (TYPES_FILE 'method'); 'sensitivity_base_module' gives the counts with its names for the rules that use it. direct: the count of names in the rule file. not_in_sqlfluff: names that are not a type of the sqlfluff 4.4.0 grammar (TYPES_FILE sqlfluff_types). renamed_in_t3: names in a T3 group key of the classes ['renamed', 'leaf_type', 'keyword_vs_identifier'] (sqruff gives another type than sqlfluff at the same span). A key gives the 2 sides of a rename, and some are generic types (for example keyword, expression): the renamed counts are upper bounds. differ: the count of names in one of the 2 lists; differ_direct: of these, the names in the rule file. changed: not_in_sqlfluff and the names that a group key changes, of T3 (sqruff-tree-diffs.json) or of the T4 parses (sqruff-rule-parses.json); not the parent type of a key, but the 2 sqlfluff types of an unparsable key. If sqruff gave sqlfluff trees, a rule with a name in changed sees a changed tree. non_code_or_meta: the names of non-code and meta types (whitespace, newline, comments, indent, dedent, implicit, and others). The T3 dialect trees are code_only (the sqlfluff dialect test compares to_tuple(code_only=True)), thus they show no difference of these types. The T4 parses have them, but only for the SQL of the failed rule, autofix, and templater cases. Thus for these names, changed is a lower bound. t3_cases: the T3 cases (of 763) with a group key that changes a name of the rule. Limits: the names come from the source text, not from the calls at run time; a helper module can name a type for one caller and not for another; a rule also reads the parent and child order of a segment, which a name does not show.

estimates.note: Estimates: the helper modules come from a static closure of the 'use' items, not from the calls. The renamed counts are upper bounds. For non-code and meta names, changed is a lower bound: the rules that see no changed tree can see one on other SQL. direct, differ_direct, and the rule file names are measurements of the source text.
